doc.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: What music means: dance, smiles and memory
summary: Heard says his feeling about playing is unchanged since his first job; music makes people smile and dance, and tunes bring back memories of marriage and church.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Well that’s okay. What was your first professional experience like, and did you think after that happened that you wanted to continue with that kind of thing? Did you want to be a musician after that?
Oh I had that same kind of feeling today, it never left me — the first experience and the way it is now, it’s the same.
And what is it like? I mean it’s like great for you?

Making somebody smile or tap their foot, like move their body, want to get up and dance. That’s music. Add some of the creator I guess, a little bit of that’s in there, you know. But it’s all about dance, shall I say, and sex.
Well you know music has — there’s a lot of babies that happened by — as a result of listening to music.
People associate that, that’s right, with certain songs, that’s right.
When you get older and you’re married forty years, fifty years, you hear that tune that you first met your wife or whatever with, you know what I mean? You go to church, there’s the music.
Music is a huge part of church.
